readings.title: The Return to Mitsrayim
readings.subtitle: Moses Obays the Command
readings.text: [Exodus 4:18] And Mosheh went and returned to Yithro his father-in-law, and said to him, “Please let me go and return to my brothers who are in Mitsrayim, and see whether they are still alive.” And Yithro said to Mosheh, “Go in peace.” [19] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh in Midyan, <dq>“Go, return to Mitsrayim, for all the men are dead who sought your life.”</dq> [20] And Mosheh took his wife and his sons and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the land of Mitsrayim. And Mosheh took the rod of <dn>Elohim</dn> in his hand. [21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“As you go back to Mitsrayim, see that you do all those wonders before Pharaoh which <dn>I</dn> have put in your hand. But <dn>I</dn> am going to strengthen his heart, so that he does not let the people go.</dq> [22] <dq>“And you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Yisra’el is <dn>My</dn> son, <dn>My</dn> first-born.</dq> [23] <dq>“So <dn>I</dn> say to you, let <dn>My</dn> son go to serve <dn>Me</dn>. But if you refuse to let him go, see, <dn>I</dn> am killing your son, your first-born.” ’ ”</dq> [24] And it came to be on the way, in the encampment, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> met him and sought to kill him. [25] Then Tsipporah took a sharp stone and cut off the foreskin of her son and cast it at his feet, and said, “You are indeed a bridegroom of blood to me!” [26] So <dn>He</dn> let him alone. Then she said, “A bridegroom of blood,” because of the circumcision. [27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Aharon, <dq>“Go into the wilderness to meet Mosheh.”</dq> So he went and met him on the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and kissed him. [28] And Mosheh told Aharon all the words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who had sent him, and all the signs which <dn>He</dn> had commanded him. [29] And Mosheh and Aharon went and gathered together all the elders of the children of Yisra’el. [30] And Aharon spoke all the words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had spoken to Mosheh. And he did the signs before the eyes of the people. [31] And the people believed. And when they heard that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had visited the children of Yisra’el and that <dn>He</dn> had looked on their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.

readings.title: Pharaoh’s Defiance
readings.subtitle: Bricks Without Straw
readings.text: [Exodus 5:1] And afterward Mosheh and Aharon went in and said to Pharaoh, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH Elohim</dn> of Yisra’el, <dq>‘Let <dn>My</dn> people go, so that they celebrate a festival to <dn>Me</dn> in the wilderness.’ ”</dq> [2] But Pharaoh said, “Who is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that I should obey <dn>His</dn> voice to let Yisra’el go? I do not know <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, nor am I going to let Yisra’el go.” [3] And they said, “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of the Hebhrews has met with us. Please, let us go three days’ journey into the wilderness and slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, lest <dn>He</dn> fall upon us with pestilence or with the sword.” [4] And the sovereign of Mitsrayim said to them, “Mosheh and Aharon, why do you take the people from their work? Get back to your burdens.” [5] And Pharaoh said, “See, the people of the land are many now, and you make them cease from their burdens!” [6] And the same day Pharaoh commanded the taskmasters of the people and their officers, saying, [7] “You are no longer to give the people straw to make bricks as before. Let them go and gather straw for themselves. [8] “And lay on them the required amount of bricks which they made before, do not reduce it. For they are idle, that is why they cry out, saying, ‘Let us go and slaughter to our <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ [9] “Let more work be laid on the men, so that they labor in it, and let them not pay attention to words of falsehood.” [10] And the taskmasters of the people and their officers went out and spoke to the people, saying, “Thus said Pharaoh, ‘I am not giving you straw. [11] ‘Go, get straw for yourselves, wherever you find it, for your work is not to be reduced at all.’ ” [12] And the people were scattered in all the land of Mitsrayim to gather stubble for straw. [13] And the taskmasters were hurrying them, saying, “Finish your work, the daily amount, as when there was straw.” [14] And the officers of the children of Yisra’el, whom Pharaoh’s taskmasters had set over them, were beaten and were asked, “Why have you not finished your required amount of bricks both yesterday and today, as before?” [15] Then the officers of the children of Yisra’el came and cried out to Pharaoh, saying, “Why do you treat your servants this way? [16] “No straw is given to your servants, and they say to us, ‘Make bricks!’ And see, your servants are beaten, but the fault is with your own people.” [17] But he said, “You are idle! Idle! That is why you say, ‘Let us go and slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ [18] “So now, go, work. And straw is not given to you, but you are to deliver the required amount of bricks.” [19] And the officers of the children of Yisra’el saw that they were in an evil state after it was said, “Do not reduce your daily amount of bricks.” [20] And as they came out from Pharaoh, they met Mosheh and Aharon who stood there to meet them. [21] And they said to them, “Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> look on you and judge, because you have made us a loathsome smell in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants, to give a sword in their hand to kill us.” [22] And Mosheh returned to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “<dn>Lord</dn>, why have <dn>You</dn> done evil to this people? Why did <dn>You</dn> send me? [23] “For since I came to Pharaoh to speak in <dn>Your</dn> Name, he has done evil to this people, and <dn>You</dn> have not delivered <dn>Your</dn> people at all!”

readings.title: The Promise of Deliverance
readings.subtitle: A Covenant Remembered
readings.text: [Exodus 6:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Now you shall see what <dn>I</dn> do to Pharaoh, for with a strong hand he shall let them go, and with a strong hand he shall drive them out of his land.”</dq> [2] And <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke to Mosheh and said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> appeared to Abraham, to Yitshaq, and to Ya‘aqobh, as <dn>El Shaddai</dn>. And by <dn>My</dn> Name <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>I</dn> was not known to them.</dq> [4] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> also established <dn>My</dn> covenant with them, to give them the land of Kena‘an, the land of their sojournings, in which they sojourned.</dq> [5] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> have also heard the groaning of the children of Yisra’el whom the Mitsrites are enslaving, and <dn>I</dn> have remembered <dn>My</dn> covenant.</dq> [6] <dq>“Say, therefore, to the children of Yisra’el, ‘<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> shall bring you out from under the burdens of the Mitsrites, and shall deliver you from their enslavement, and shall redeem you with an outstretched arm and with great judgments,</dq> [7] <dq>‘and shall take you as <dn>My</dn> people, and <dn>I</dn> shall be your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> who is bringing you out from under the burdens of the Mitsrites.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And <dn>I</dn> shall bring you into the land which <dn>I</dn> swore to give to Abraham, to Yitshaq, and to Ya‘aqobh, and shall give it to you as an inheritance. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq> [9] And Mosheh spoke thus to the children of Yisra’el, but they did not listen to Mosheh, because of shortness of spirit and from hard slavery. [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [11] <dq>“Go in, speak to Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, to let the children of Yisra’el go out of his land.”</dq> [12] And Mosheh spoke before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “See, the children of Yisra’el have not listened to me. Why then would Pharaoh listen to me, for I am of uncircumcised lips?” [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, and gave them a command for the children of Yisra’el and for Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, to bring the children of Yisra’el out of the land of Mitsrayim. [14] These are the heads of their fathers’ houses: The sons of Re’uḇen, the first-born of Yisra’el: Ḥanoḵ and Pallu, Ḥetsron and Karmi. These are the clans of Re’uḇen. [15] And the sons of Shim‘on: Yemu’el and Yamim, and Ohad and Yaḵin, and Tsoḥar and Sha’ul the son of a Kena‘anite woman. These are the clans of Shim‘on. [16] And these are the names of the sons of Lewi according to their generations: Gershon and Qehath and Merari. And the years of the life of Lewi were one hundred and thirty-seven. [17] The sons of Gershon: Liḇni and Shim‘i according to their clans. [18] And the sons of Qehath: Amram and Yitshar, and Ḥeḇron and Uzzi’el. And the years of the life of Qehath were one hundred and thirty-three. [19] And the sons of Merari: Maḥli and Mushi. These are the clans of Lewi according to their generations. [20] And Amram took for himself Yoḵeḇeḏ his father’s sister as wife, and she bore him Aharon and Mosheh. And the years of the life of Amram were one hundred and thirty-seven. [21] And the sons of Yitshar: Qoraḥ and Nepheg and Ziḵri. [22] And the sons of Uzzi’el: Misha’el and Eltsaphan and Sithri. [23] And Aharon took for himself Elisheḇa, daughter of Amminaḏaḇ, sister of Naḥshon, as wife, and she bore him Naḏaḇ and Aḇihu, El‘azar and Ithamar. [24] And the sons of Qoraḥ: Assir and Elqanah and Aḇiyasaph. These are the clans of the Qorḥites. [25] And El‘azar, Aharon’s son, took for himself one of the daughters of Puti’el as wife, and she bore him Pineḥas. These are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Lewites according to their clans. [26] This is Aharon and Mosheh, to whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Bring out the children of Yisra’el from the land of Mitsrayim according to their divisions.”</dq> [27] They were the ones who spoke to Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim, to bring out the children of Yisra’el from Mitsrayim. This is Mosheh and Aharon. [28] And it came to be, on the day when <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh in the land of Mitsrayim, [29] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Speak to Pharaoh sovereign of Mitsrayim all that <dn>I</dn> say to you.”</dq> [30] And Mosheh said before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “See, I am of uncircumcised lips, and why would Pharaoh listen to me?”

readings.title: The Confrontation
readings.subtitle: Elohim to Pharaoh
readings.text: [Exodus 7:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> have made you an Elohim to Pharaoh, and Aharon your brother shall be your prophet.</dq> [2] <dq>“You shall speak all that <dn>I</dn> command you. And Aharon your brother shall speak to Pharaoh to let the children of Yisra’el go out of his land.</dq> [3] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> am going to strengthen the heart of Pharaoh, and shall multiply <dn>My</dn> signs and <dn>My</dn> wonders in the land of Mitsrayim.</dq> [4] <dq>“And Pharaoh is not going to listen to you, and <dn>I</dn> shall lay <dn>My</dn> hand on Mitsrayim and bring <dn>My</dn> divisions, <dn>My</dn> people the children of Yisra’el, out of the land of Mitsrayim by great judgments.</dq> [5] <dq>“And the Mitsrites shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, when <dn>I</dn> stretch out <dn>My</dn> hand on Mitsrayim and bring out the children of Yisra’el from their midst.”</dq> [6] And Mosheh and Aharon did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded them, so they did. [7] And Mosheh was eighty years old and Aharon eighty-three years old when they spoke to Pharaoh. [8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying, [9] <dq>“When Pharaoh speaks to you, saying, ‘Show a miracle for yourselves,’ then you shall say to Aharon, ‘Take your rod and throw it before Pharaoh, and let it become a serpent.’ ”</dq> [10] So Mosheh and Aharon went in to Pharaoh, and they did so, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded. And Aharon threw his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent. [11] But Pharaoh also called the wise men and the enchanters. And they, the magicians of Mitsrayim, also did so with their magic. [12] For every man threw down his rod, and they became serpents. But Aharon’s rod swallowed up their rods. [13] And Pharaoh’s heart was strengthened, and he did not listen to them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had said.
